title: How Gentle Tapping on the Shin Heals the Brain - Nautilus
gist: Researchers at Southern Medical University in China gave mice and pigs brain injuries, then rhythmically tapped their shin bones for five days to test whether bones can help heal the brain. The idea reverses a known effect in which traumatic brain injury speeds bone healing. The excerpt gives no results beyond the headline claim.

insights.claim: Doctors have long seen that people with traumatic brain injuries heal bone faster, because damaged brain cells release protein-filled vesicles that stimulate bone stem cells.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Two-way bone-brain signaling could open new therapeutic and medical-device approaches.
insights.quote: When some brain cells are damaged, they release vesicles filled with proteins that travel to the bone stem cells and stimulate growth
